title: Aviation mechanic inspection authorization practice questions
description: Practice questions on the FAA inspection authorization: eligibility, the written test, duration, renewal activities, privileges (14 CFR 65.91-65.95).

questions.question: An applicant shows that every requirement of 65.91 is met. What does 65.91(b) say about that applicant?

options.A: The applicant may receive an inspection authorization only if the Flight Standards office decides one is needed in the area
options.B: The applicant is entitled to an inspection authorization
options.C: The applicant must first work for one year under the supervision of another inspection authorization holder
options.D: The applicant must also hold at least a private pilot certificate

questions.explanation: 65.91(b) states: "An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.91, Inspection authorization (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 65.91(c)(2), what must an applicant have been actively engaged in for at least the 2-year period before the date of application?

options.A: Flying aircraft as pilot in command
options.B: Teaching aviation maintenance classes
options.C: Designing aircraft parts for a manufacturer
options.D: Maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter

questions.explanation: The applicant must "Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.91, Inspection authorization (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Base, equipment and the written test
questions.question: What does 65.91(c)(3) require of the applicant's fixed base of operations?

options.A: It must be the place where every inspection under the authorization is performed
options.B: It must be located at a certificated repair station
options.C: It must be a place where the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week; it need not be where the inspection authority is exercised
options.D: It must be on an airport with an operating control tower

questions.explanation: The applicant must "Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.91, Inspection authorization (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Base, equipment and the written test
questions.question: What is the written test in 65.91(c)(5) about?

options.A: The applicant's ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43
options.B: The applicant's ability to fly an aircraft on a test flight after maintenance
options.C: The applicant's knowledge of aircraft design engineering and stress analysis
options.D: The applicant's knowledge of running a business at a fixed base of operations

questions.explanation: The applicant must "Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.91, Inspection authorization (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Base, equipment and the written test
questions.question: What does 65.91(c)(4) require an applicant for an inspection authorization to have available?

options.A: A hangar owned by the applicant at the fixed base of operations
options.B: A written approval from a certificated repair station
options.C: The equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance
options.D: An aircraft the applicant may use for test flights after inspections

questions.explanation: The applicant must "Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.91, Inspection authorization (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Duration and when an IA stops being effective
questions.question: Under 65.92(b), which of these events makes an inspection authorization cease to be effective?

options.A: The authorization is surrendered, suspended, or revoked
options.B: The holder's lost mechanic certificate is replaced
options.C: The holder starts using a different telephone number at the fixed base
options.D: The holder begins inspecting aircraft away from the fixed base

questions.explanation: An inspection authorization "ceases to be effective whenever any of the following occurs", including "The authorization is surrendered, suspended, or revoked."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.92, Inspection authorization: Duration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Duration and when an IA stops being effective
questions.question: Under 65.92(a), the holder may exercise the privileges of an inspection authorization only while holding what?

options.A: At least a private pilot certificate
options.B: A job with a certificated repair station
options.C: A mechanic certificate with either a currently effective airframe rating or a currently effective powerplant rating
options.D: A currently effective mechanic certificate with both a currently effective airframe rating and a currently effective powerplant rating

questions.explanation: The holder "may exercise the privileges of that authorization only while he holds a currently effective mechanic certificate with both a currently effective airframe rating and a currently effective powerplant rating."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.92, Inspection authorization: Duration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Duration and when an IA stops being effective
questions.question: An inspection authorization holder no longer has a fixed base of operation. What does 65.92(b) say happens to the authorization?

options.A: It stays effective until the next March 31
options.B: It ceases to be effective
options.C: It stays effective as long as the mechanic certificate is effective
options.D: It stays effective for 90 days

questions.explanation: An inspection authorization "ceases to be effective whenever any of the following occurs", including "The holder no longer has a fixed base of operation."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.92, Inspection authorization: Duration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Duration and when an IA stops being effective
questions.question: Under 65.92(c), what must the holder of a suspended or revoked inspection authorization do?

options.A: Return it to the Administrator upon the Administrator's request
options.B: Destroy it
options.C: Keep it until its expiration date
options.D: Send it to the National Transportation Safety Board

questions.explanation: The holder of an inspection authorization that is suspended or revoked "shall, upon the Administrator's request, return it to the Administrator."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.92, Inspection authorization: Duration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Except as provided in 65.93(d), when and where does 65.93(a) say an applicant must present evidence for renewal of an inspection authorization?

options.A: During the month of January of each even-numbered year, at any FAA office
options.B: At any time during the 2-year period, at a certificated repair station
options.C: During the month of March of each odd-numbered year, at the responsible Flight Standards office
options.D: Within 30 days after the expiration date, by mail to the Administrator

questions.explanation: Except as provided in paragraph (d), the applicant "must present evidence during the month of March of each odd-numbered year, at the responsible Flight Standards office".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.93, Inspection authorization: Renewal (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What must the renewal evidence in 65.93(a) show?

options.A: That the applicant has passed the written test again
options.B: That the applicant still meets the requirements of § 65.91(c)(1) through (4)
options.C: That the applicant has held the authorization for at least 3 years
options.D: That the applicant works for an air carrier

questions.explanation: The applicant must present evidence "that the applicant still meets the requirements of § 65.91(c)(1) through (4)."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.93, Inspection authorization: Renewal (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 65.93(a), what deadline does the rule set for showing completion of one of the activities in (a)(1) through (5) for the first year of the 2-year period?

options.A: By December 31 of the first year
options.B: Within 90 days after the authorization is issued
options.C: Only once, at any time during the 2-year period
options.D: By March 31 of the first year of the 2-year inspection authorization period

questions.explanation: The applicant must show "completion of one of the activities in paragraphs (a)(1) through (5) of this section by March 31 of the first year of the 2-year inspection authorization period, and completion of one of the five activities during the second year of the 2-year period".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.93, Inspection authorization: Renewal (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An inspection authorization holder completed one of the activities in 65.93(a)(1) through (5) before March 31 of the first year. What does 65.93(a) require for the second year of the 2-year period?

options.A: Completion of one of the five activities during the second year
options.B: Nothing more, because the first-year activity covers both years
options.C: Completion of two of the activities during the second year
options.D: Passing the written test in 65.91(c)(5) again

questions.explanation: The applicant must show completion of one activity "by March 31 of the first year of the 2-year inspection authorization period, and completion of one of the five activities during the second year of the 2-year period".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.93, Inspection authorization: Renewal (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An inspection authorization took effect 60 days before March 31 of an even-numbered year. What does 65.93(b)(2) say about the activities in paragraphs (a)(1) through (5)?

options.A: The holder must complete two of the activities in the first year instead of one
options.B: The holder must pass an oral test from an FAA inspector before exercising any privileges
options.C: The holder must complete one activity within 60 days
options.D: The holder need not comply with them for the first year of the 2-year inspection authorization period

questions.explanation: An inspection authorization in effect "for less than 90 days before March 31 of an even-numbered year need not comply with paragraphs (a)(1) through (5) of this section for the first year of the 2-year inspection authorization period."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.93, Inspection authorization: Renewal (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An inspection authorization has been in effect for less than 90 days before the expiration date. What does 65.93(b)(1) say?

options.A: The holder must complete two of the activities instead of one
options.B: The holder must pass the written test again
options.C: The holder need not comply with paragraphs (a)(1) through (5)
options.D: The holder may not renew until the next odd-numbered year

questions.explanation: The holder of an inspection authorization that has been in effect "for less than 90 days before the expiration date need not comply with paragraphs (a)(1) through (5) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.93, Inspection authorization: Renewal (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A holder did not complete one of the activities by March 31 of the first year. Under 65.93(c), what lets the holder resume exercising inspection authorization privileges?

options.A: Waiting until April 1 of the second year
options.B: Passing an oral test from an FAA inspector to determine that the applicant's knowledge of the applicable regulations and standards is current
options.C: Getting a signed statement from an aircraft owner
options.D: Notifying the Flight Standards office in writing of the delay

questions.explanation: Such a holder "may not exercise inspection authorization privileges after March 31 of the first year" but "may resume exercising inspection authorization privileges after passing an oral test from an FAA inspector to determine that the applicant's knowledge of the applicable regulations and standards is current."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.93, Inspection authorization: Renewal (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An inspection authorization holder is asked to inspect and approve for return to service, after a major alteration, an airplane that an air carrier maintains in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121. How does 65.95(a)(1) treat that airplane?

options.A: It is excepted from the holder's privilege to inspect and approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration
options.B: It is covered, provided the holder also performs an annual inspection on it
options.C: It is covered, provided the air carrier's director of maintenance co-signs the approval
options.D: It is covered only if the major alteration was done at the holder's fixed base of operations

questions.explanation: The privilege covers "any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter)" after a major repair or major alteration.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.95, Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 65.95(a)(1), on what condition may the holder inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft after a major repair or major alteration?

options.A: If the holder did the work personally
options.B: If the work was done at the holder's fixed base of operation
options.C: If the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator
options.D: If the aircraft owner signs the approval

questions.explanation: The holder may approve the work "if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.95, Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Keeping the IA available and changing base
questions.question: When exercising the privileges of an inspection authorization, for whom must the holder keep it available for inspection under 65.95(b)?

options.A: Only the responsible Flight Standards office
options.B: Any passenger of the aircraft
options.C: The manufacturer of the aircraft
options.D: The aircraft owner and the mechanic submitting the aircraft, repair, or alteration for approval (if any)

questions.explanation: The holder "shall keep it available for inspection by the aircraft owner, the mechanic submitting the aircraft, repair, or alteration for approval (if any)".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.95, Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Keeping the IA available and changing base
questions.question: Pat, an inspection authorization holder, moves the fixed base of operation to a new city and phones the Flight Standards office for that area to mention the move. Under 65.95(c), what must Pat still do before exercising the privileges of the authorization?

options.A: Apply for a new inspection authorization and pass the written test again
options.B: Notify the responsible Flight Standards office or International Field Office for the area in which the new base is located, in writing, of the change
options.C: Notify the office for the area of the old base, in writing, of the change
options.D: Wait 90 days after the move

questions.explanation: The holder "may not exercise the privileges of the authorization until he has notified the responsible Flight Standards office or International Field Office for the area in which the new base is located, in writing, of the change."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 65.95, Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)
